conventions.date_precision: kept as stated by the source; a year is never 1 January

events.title: Development Corporation of British Columbia Act assented to, establishing the British Columbia Development Corporation

evidence.locator: SBC 1973, c. 27, assent heading; s. 2 (corporation established); s. 37 (commencement)

events.interpretation_notes: The Act came into force by proclamation and was made retroactive to 31 March 1973, the date the body record uses. Its capital was $25 million in $100 shares bought by the Minister of Finance (s. 3).

events.title: BCDC’s four-prism emblem beside its four-line name, in an advertisement for business-management courses in the Aldergrove Star
events.interpretation_notes: Documented use by this date, not its introduction; the designer is not known. The same advertisement also sets the emblem small beside an all-capital sans-serif name. Repeated in the Aldergrove Star and the Peninsula Times of 14 January 1976.

events.title: The First Capital City Development Company Limited incorporated as BCDC’s wholly owned subsidiary to direct and manage the redevelopment of downtown and waterfront New Westminster

evidence.locator: BC Ombudsman Special Report No. 9 (Supreme Court of Canada judgment), PDF page 26, judgment page 5

events.interpretation_notes: New Westminster’s Heritage Resource Inventory: Downtown also calls it a wholly owned BCDC subsidiary. The New Westminster Redevelopment Act, 1979 names the company and its agreement with the city (approved by council on 18 December 1978). Its redevelopment became Westminster Quay; its own mark was registered as a trademark (CIPO 0460347, filed 22 October 1980).

events.title: BCDC files its four-square “The Development Corporation” mark as a trademark, claiming use since at least 31 March 1980
events.interpretation_notes: The claimed first use is the owner’s claim, not a verified date. Two official marks of the same design in sans-serif followed in 1981 (0901351, 0901352), and the four squares alone were registered in 1983 (0494945). All four were cancelled or withdrawn in late 1989.

events.title: All BCDC’s property, assets, obligations and liabilities transferred to British Columbia Enterprise Corporation

evidence.locator: British Columbia Enterprise Corporation Financial Restructuring Act, SBC 1987 c. 39, s. 2 (B.C. Reg. 289/87)

events.interpretation_notes: The same day BC Place Ltd. was renamed British Columbia Enterprise Corporation. References to BCDC in its commercial paper became references to BCEC, and government guarantees of its securities stood. BCDC’s trademarks passed with its assets: Lonsdale Quay Market & Design (CIPO 0530417) records an assignment to BCEC effective 31 March 1987 and to Lonsdale Quay Market Corporation on 28 June 1990.
